pr_title: cleanup: extract generateSelector from Validate method in job strategy
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
`Validate` calls `generateSelector` which adds labels. This is wrong - `Validate` is not supposed to modify objects! This should be done from PrepareFor* hooks instead. A side-effect of this is that any update operation will set these labels, which seems like a benefit but is hidden in a place where nobody will NEVER think to look.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Partially fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116137 as per @thockin comment https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116137#issuecomment-1448520671

A followup PR will be created to address the second issue mentioned by @thockin.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
NONE
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

issue_context.title: General Validation Cleanup for Jobs
issue_context.body:
@thockin pointed out in a review that the way we generate selectors for the Job controller is a bit odd.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114930#pullrequestreview-1316052164

/kind cleanup
/sig apps

Copying here for simplicty:

Problem 1:  `Validate` calls `generateSelector`  which adds labels.  This is wrong - `Validate` is not supposed to modify objects!  This should be done from `PrepareFor*` hooks instead.  A side-effect of this is that any update operation will set these labels, which seems like a benefit but is hidden in a place I would NEVER think to look.

I would retool all of this.  `PrepareForCreate` should call `generateSelectorIfNeeded`, which checks the `manual` flag and sets the labels.  It's not clear to me whether that should happen from `PrepareForUpdate` or not.  It's easy, but a bit unusual (to set unrelated fields) and low-value (I think).

Problem 2: `Validate` says `if job.Spec.ManualSelector == nil || *job.Spec.ManualSelector == false` - this is wrong.  That field should be recognized as `nil` in pkg/apis/batch/v1/defaults.go and assigned a value.  You should not be nil-checking fields all over the place and inferring their default values.  It seems innocuous on a bool, but imagine an int or string field - you'd have the default value sprinkled all over the codebase.

This could be 2 distinct PRs

Hi all,

This looks like a good first issue, I'll be more than happy to take a stab at it.

/assign dejanzele

The Validate vs. PrepareForCreate part should be straight forward (will need tests).

The defaults parts may require other test cases to be updated so that the field is never nil - not hard but may be a bit tedious. :)

Hello @thockin,

Sorry for the delay, I finally want to dedicate time to do the cleanup which you have mentioned in a comment above.

I will follow your advice and create 2 separate PRs.

First one I have created is about extracting the `generateSelector` method.

review_comments: I think we should cover this by tests in `TestJobStrategy_PrepareForCreate`.
@mimowo I have added a test case in `TestJobStrategy_PrepareForCreate`, can you please review again?
These are valid labels that we add to `ObjectMeta` but they don't have to be in the selector. Please add back.

I think you should keep this the same to minimize the diff.  No reason to change this.  

I think it makes sense to call it valid as you aren't really testing these values.

Actually, I want to change the podSpec in all of the wanted jobs, as I want to assert that each one contains the added labels.

I can rename it to `validXXX` but my point was that I create another `podTemplate` which contains the expected labels, hence why I named it `expectedPodTemplateSpec`

I would minimize the changes honestly.  In this case, we have the `Selector` is set to `validSelector` but `Template` has `expectedPodTemplateSpec`.  We have the code as `wantJob` for expected so I don't think you need to change it.

It will work just the same if we use `validPodTemplateSpec`, but then the test works because of a side-effect that we pass the `validPodTemplateSpec` as reference and the `generateSelectors` function adds the missing fields.
IMHO it is more explicit this way and clearer what is expected.

My issue is that you have some cases where the values are valid and others that are expected.

```
					Selector:         validSelector,
					Template:         expectedPodTemplateSpec,
```

Its a nonblocking nit.  Just a suggestion because now we have different names for different items in the expected spec.
